# CLI

<!-- Generated by `tond docs cli` from the CLI's own definitions (run `just docs-gen`). Do not edit by hand. -->

`tond` is the command-line interface to a Tond server. It ships with every install (`/usr/local/bin/tond`) and in every release tarball.

**On the server**, run it as root: it talks to tond-server over the root-only Unix socket `/opt/tond/data/tond.sock` and needs no credentials.

**From anywhere else** (your laptop, CI), pass the server's URL and an [API token](/concepts/access): `--server https://tond.example.com --token tond_pat_…`, or set `TOND_SERVER` and `TOND_TOKEN`. What the token may do depends on its scopes.

**For scripts and agents:**

- `--json` works on every command: stdout holds one JSON document (the result), and a failure prints one JSON error line on stderr.
- Exit codes tell failures apart (not found, denied, conflict, deploy failed, server unavailable…): see [Exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) or run `tond help exit-codes`.
- Destructive commands ask for confirmation in a terminal and refuse without one; pass `--yes` in CI.
- `tond apps deploy` and `tond apps push` wait for the deploy to finish and exit non-zero if it fails; `--no-wait` returns as soon as it is queued.
- Mutating requests carry an idempotency key, so a retried command never acts twice; `--idempotency-key` (or `TOND_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`) sets it.
- `tond completions bash|zsh|fish` prints a shell completion script, e.g. `tond completions bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/tond`.

Every command prints `--help`, and `tond help <command>` does the same.

## Global options

These work with every command.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--server <SERVER>` | Server URL to connect to over HTTP(S) instead of the local socket (requires --token). Env: `TOND_SERVER`. |
| `--token <TOKEN>` | API token (tond_pat_…) for --server connections. Env: `TOND_TOKEN`. |
| `--socket <SOCKET>` | Path to tond-server's local Unix socket (used when --server is not set). Default: `/opt/tond/data/tond.sock`. Env: `TOND_SOCKET_PATH`. |
| `--json` | Print machine-readable JSON on stdout (errors as one JSON line on stderr). |
| `--idempotency-key <IDEMPOTENCY_KEY>` | Idempotency-Key sent with mutating requests (default: a new UUID per request). Repeating a command with the same key returns the first result instead of acting twice. Env: `TOND_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`. |

## tond apps

Manage apps

```text
tond apps <COMMAND>
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond apps list` | List all deployed apps |
| `tond apps create` | Create a new app |
| `tond apps deploy` | Deploy an app (build & start from stored source); waits and streams the build unless --no-wait. Exits 6 if the build or deploy fails |
| `tond apps push` | Deploy the current directory to an app (tar + upload); waits like `deploy` |
| `tond apps info` | Show app details |
| `tond apps logs` | View app logs |
| `tond apps stop` | Stop an app |
| `tond apps start` | Start a stopped app |
| `tond apps restart` | Restart an app |
| `tond apps delete` | Delete an app (asks first; --yes to skip) |
| `tond apps env` | Set environment variables |
| `tond apps domain` | Set custom domain for an app |
| `tond apps health` | Configure health checks for an app |
| `tond apps drain-timeout` | Set the graceful-deploy drain timeout for an app |
| `tond apps deployments` | Show deployment history for an app |
| `tond apps rollback` | Roll back an app to its previous deployment (asks first; --yes to skip) |
| `tond apps git-key` | Show or generate the SSH deploy key for an app |
| `tond apps git-webhook` | Manage webhook URL and auto-deploy settings for an app |
| `tond apps volume` | Manage persistent volumes for an app |
| `tond apps previews` | Manage preview deployments for an app |

### tond apps list

List all deployed apps

```text
tond apps list
```

### tond apps create

Create a new app

```text
tond apps create [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | App name (alphanumeric + hyphens). |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--template <TEMPLATE>` | Curated in-repo template to use for app creation. |
| `-t, --source-type <SOURCE_TYPE>` | Source type: git, image. Default: `git`. |
| `-s, --source <SOURCE>` | Git URL or Docker image. |
| `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` | Git branch. Default: `main`. |
| `-p, --port <PORT>` | Container port. Default: `3000`. |
| `-d, --domain <DOMAIN>` | Custom domain. |
| `--env <ENV>` | Environment variable override in KEY=VALUE format. Repeat for multiple values. |
| `--memory-mb <MEMORY_MB>` | Memory limit in megabytes (default: 256). |
| `--cpus <CPUS>` | CPU limit as a float (e.g. 0.5 = half a core, 1.0 = one core; default: 0.5). |
| `--health-path <HEALTH_PATH>` | HTTP path for health checks (e.g. /health); omit to disable. |
| `--health-interval <HEALTH_INTERVAL>` | Seconds between health check polls (default: 30). |
| `--health-threshold <HEALTH_THRESHOLD>` | Consecutive failures before marking unhealthy (default: 3). |
| `--drain-timeout <DRAIN_TIMEOUT>` | Seconds to wait for the new container to pass health checks before cutting traffic over during a graceful redeploy (default: 30). |
| `--build-method <BUILD_METHOD>` | Build method for git/tarball sources: tbuild (server default) or dockerfile. "tbuild" scans the repo and auto-generates a Dockerfile. Only sent when given, since the server rejects a build method for image sources. |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip interactive prompts and fail if required template inputs are missing. |

### tond apps deploy

Deploy an app (build & start from stored source); waits and streams the build unless --no-wait. Exits 6 if the build or deploy fails

```text
tond apps deploy [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<APP>` | App name or ID. |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--wait` | Stream the build and exit non-zero if it fails (the default). |
| `--no-wait` | Return as soon as the deploy is queued and print the deployment id. |

### tond apps push

Deploy the current directory to an app (tar + upload); waits like `deploy`

```text
tond apps push [OPTIONS] <APP>
```

| --- | --- |
| `<APP>` | App name or ID. |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--wait` | Stream the build and exit non-zero if it fails (the default). |
| `--no-wait` | Return as soon as the deploy is queued and print the deployment id. |

## tond update

Update Tond to the latest release (or --version), exactly like System → Updates in the dashboard: tond-server takes a full snapshot, then installs the release in the background, migrates the database, checks that everything is healthy and rolls back automatically if not. This command follows the progress and exits non-zero unless the update succeeded.

For 7 days after an update, --rollback returns to the previous version.

```text
tond update [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--rollback` | Go back to the version before the last update (within 7 days). |
| `--check` | Only report the running and the latest version, and the changelog. |
| `--skip-snapshot` | Don't take a snapshot first (not recommended). |
| `--force` | Reinstall the running version, or install an older release. |
| `--direct` | Update without tond-server: download, verify and run update.sh here (also used when tond-server is down; no snapshot is taken). |
| `--dry-run` | Show what update.sh would do, without changing anything (implies --direct). |

View or update server-wide settings

```text
tond settings [COMMAND]
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond settings set-server-name` | Set the human-readable name for this Tond server instance |
| `tond settings set-dashboard-domain` | Set the domain used to access the Tond dashboard |
| `tond settings set-preview-domain` | Set the domain previews are served under (<slug>-<app>.<domain>) |
| `tond settings set-apps-domain` | Set the domain automatic app hostnames live under (<app>.<domain>) |
| `tond settings host-terminal` | Turn the dashboard's host terminal (a shell on this server) on or off |

### tond settings set-server-name

Set the human-readable name for this Tond server instance

```text
tond settings set-server-name <NAME>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<NAME>` | Server name (e.g. "My VPS"). Pass an empty string to clear. |

### tond settings set-dashboard-domain

Set the domain used to access the Tond dashboard

The domain is written to the database. tond-proxy picks it up within 5 seconds — no proxy restart needed.

```text
tond settings set-dashboard-domain <DOMAIN>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<DOMAIN>` | Domain name (e.g. tond.example.com). Pass an empty string to clear. |

### tond settings set-preview-domain

Set the domain previews are served under (<slug>-<app>.<domain>)

Must be a separate domain you own — not the dashboard domain, a parent or subdomain of it, or anything on the same registrable domain — with a wildcard DNS record *.<domain> pointing at this server. Previews run pull-request code, so they must not share a site with the dashboard. Previews cannot be enabled until this is set.

```text
tond settings set-preview-domain <DOMAIN>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<DOMAIN>` | Domain name (e.g. example-previews.com). Pass an empty string to clear. |

### tond settings set-apps-domain

Set the domain automatic app hostnames live under (<app>.<domain>)

Must be a separate site from the dashboard and preview domains (apps run your code; keeping them off the dashboard's site keeps them away from its cookies), with a wildcard DNS record *.<domain> pointing at this server. Without it, apps need a custom domain.

```text
tond settings set-apps-domain <DOMAIN>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<DOMAIN>` | Domain name (e.g. example-apps.com). Pass an empty string to clear. |

### tond settings host-terminal

Turn the dashboard's host terminal (a shell on this server) on or off

Off by default. It can only be switched from the server itself (this command, run as root), never from the dashboard or with an API token. When on, only admins can use it and every session asks for their password (and 2FA code).

```text
tond settings host-terminal <STATE>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<STATE>` | One of `on`, `off`. |

## tond storage-provider

Manage S3-compatible storage providers for backups

```text
tond storage-provider <COMMAND>
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond storage-provider list` | List all configured storage providers |
| `tond storage-provider create` | Create a new S3-compatible storage provider |
| `tond storage-provider test` | Test connectivity to a storage provider |
| `tond storage-provider delete` | Delete a storage provider (asks first) |

### tond storage-provider list

List all configured storage providers

```text
tond storage-provider list
```

### tond storage-provider create

Create a new S3-compatible storage provider

```text
tond storage-provider create [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <NAME>` | Human-readable label for this provider. Required. |
| `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>` | S3-compatible endpoint URL (e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com). Required. |
| `--region <REGION>` | AWS region (e.g. us-east-1). Required. |
| `--bucket <BUCKET>` | Bucket name. Required. |
| `--prefix <PREFIX>` | Key prefix inside the bucket (optional). |
| `--key-id <KEY_ID>` | Access key ID. Required. |
| `--secret <SECRET>` | Secret access key. Required. |

### tond storage-provider test

Test connectivity to a storage provider

```text
tond storage-provider test <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | Storage provider ID. |

### tond storage-provider delete

Delete a storage provider (asks first)

```text
tond storage-provider delete [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | Storage provider ID. |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Don't ask for confirmation (required when stdin is not a terminal). |

## tond snapshot

Manage snapshots and backup configuration

```text
tond snapshot <COMMAND>
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond snapshot create` | Create a manual full snapshot |
| `tond snapshot list` | List snapshots |
| `tond snapshot restore` | Restore a full snapshot (asks first; the server restarts) |
| `tond snapshot rollback` | Roll back a single app or database to a snapshot state (no server restart; asks first) |
| `tond snapshot delete` | Delete a snapshot (asks first) |
| `tond snapshot config` | Backup configuration sub-commands |

### tond snapshot create

Create a manual full snapshot

```text
tond snapshot create [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <NAME>` | Optional human-readable label for this snapshot. |

### tond snapshot list

List snapshots

```text
tond snapshot list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--app <APP>` | Filter to snapshots for a specific app name. |

### tond snapshot restore

Restore a full snapshot (asks first; the server restarts)

```text
tond snapshot restore [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | Snapshot ID to restore from. |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Don't ask for confirmation (required when stdin is not a terminal). |

### tond snapshot rollback

Roll back a single app or database to a snapshot state (no server restart; asks first)

```text
tond snapshot rollback [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | Snapshot ID to roll back from. |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--app <APP>` | Name of the app to roll back. |
| `--database <DATABASE>` | Name of the managed database to restore. |
| `-y, --yes` | Don't ask for confirmation (required when stdin is not a terminal). |

### tond snapshot delete

Delete a snapshot (asks first)

```text
tond snapshot delete [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<ID>` | Snapshot ID to delete. |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Don't ask for confirmation (required when stdin is not a terminal). |

### tond snapshot config

Backup configuration sub-commands

```text
tond snapshot config <COMMAND>
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond snapshot config show` | Show current backup configuration |
| `tond snapshot config set` | Update backup configuration |

#### tond snapshot config show

Show current backup configuration

```text
tond snapshot config show
```

#### tond snapshot config set

Update backup configuration

```text
tond snapshot config set [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--schedule <SCHEDULE>` | Cron expression for scheduled backups (e.g. "0 3 * * *"). |
| `--retain <RETAIN>` | Number of full snapshots to retain. |
| `--pre-deploy-enabled <PRE_DEPLOY_ENABLED>` | Enable or disable pre-deploy snapshots (true/false). One of `true`, `false`. |
| `--pre-deploy-retain <PRE_DEPLOY_RETAIN>` | Number of pre-deploy snapshots to retain per app. |
| `--keep-local <KEEP_LOCAL>` | Keep a local copy of snapshots (true/false). One of `true`, `false`. |
| `--provider <PROVIDER>` | Storage provider ID to upload snapshots to (use "none" to clear). |

## tond token

Manage API tokens (scoped, expiring credentials for automation)

```text
tond token <COMMAND>
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond token create` | Create an API token and print it once |
| `tond token list` | List API tokens (yours, or every token with --all) |
| `tond token revoke` | Revoke an API token (by id, name or visible prefix; asks first) |

### tond token create

Create an API token and print it once

```text
tond token create [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <NAME>` | What the token is for (e.g. the CI workflow or machine). Required. |
| `--kind <KIND>` | personal, service, agent or ci. Default: `service`. |
| `--preset <PRESET>` | Start from a preset: readonly, deployer, agent-operator. |
| `--scope <SCOPES>` | Extra scope, e.g. apps:deploy (repeatable). |
| `--app <APPS>` | Limit the token to this app, by name or id (repeatable). |
| `--project <PROJECTS>` | Limit the token to the apps of this project (repeatable). |
| `--allow-ip <ALLOWED_IPS>` | Only accept the token from this IP or CIDR range (repeatable). |
| `--expires <EXPIRES>` | Lifetime such as 24h, 30d or 12w, or "never" (agent tokens must expire). Default: 24h for agent tokens, 90d otherwise. |

### tond token list

List API tokens (yours, or every token with --all)

```text
tond token list [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--all` | Every user's tokens (needs tokens:admin; always the case as root). |

### tond token revoke

Revoke an API token (by id, name or visible prefix; asks first)

```text
tond token revoke [OPTIONS] <TOKEN>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<TOKEN>` |  |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Don't ask for confirmation (required when stdin is not a terminal). |

## tond audit

Inspect the audit log

```text
tond audit <COMMAND>
```

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tond audit verify` | Verify the audit log's hash chain (exit status 1 if it was tampered with) |
| `tond audit log` | Show recent audit log entries, newest first |

### tond audit verify

Verify the audit log's hash chain (exit status 1 if it was tampered with)

```text
tond audit verify
```

### tond audit log

Show recent audit log entries, newest first

```text
tond audit log [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--actor <ACTOR>` | Only this actor (email, token name or "local-socket"). |
| `--action <ACTION>` | Only this action (a trailing * matches a prefix, e.g. "login*"). |
| `--limit <LIMIT>` | How many entries (1-200). Default: `50`. |

## tond completions

Print a shell completion script, e.g. `tond completions bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/tond`

```text
tond completions <SHELL>
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<SHELL>` | Shell to generate completions for. One of `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `powershell`, `zsh`. |

## tond help

Print help for a command (`tond help apps deploy`) or the exit-code table (`tond help exit-codes`)

```text
tond help [TOPIC...]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[TOPIC]` | Command path, or `exit-codes`. |
